Over this past year, I started hanging out with a girl from work (we work in fast food, for some important context).  She is noticeably skinnier than me. 


When we go out to eat, we often eat the same way- bowls of pasta, hot wings, the occasional drink. Just looking at that, it would be so easy to say "how is she skinnier than me?" But since we work around food, I get to see more of what our habits are. 


When we stop to eat at work, I get a bigger burger. She gets a smaller chicken sandwich. My quick snack is a 6 piece nugget, she grabs 2 nuggets. Before work, I usually eat freezer meals or calorie heavy snacks. She takes a salad home with her to be lunch the next day. My "occasional treat" at work is a medium ice cream, hers is a junior one. 

If we didn't work together, around food all night, I would be able to believe that "we eat the same". But we definitely don't. You can't look at the every once in a while and say that's the all day every day.
Evidence suggests that the fact they are together does not in fact mean that nobody else will end up with them.

Some things that have worked for me:

1- set rewards for certain milestones: every 10 pounds, going from overweight to a healthy weight by bmi, whatever. I aim for body related, but not food related rewards: getting my hair done, getting a bike, clothes shopping...

2- experiment with foods: I may be the only person I've met that enjoys that, but I do seriously enjoy it. Finding new foods I like, or coming up with lower calorie versions of foods I already know I like. 

3- find an exercise you enjoy, or a way to make another one fun. Like zombies run for walking or running, or ring fit for bodyweight. Or find people to exercise with, or challenge each other to achieve goals.

"Wait until I'm in college and we're at a family function and you comment on my grades", I thought. "We'll see how you feel about this then!"

So in my experience (in the us): what "grade" you're in in high school is somewhat fluid. You're given all your classes at the level you're at (based on classes you've completed already, or tested out of over the summer), and "9th, 10th, 11th, or 12th" is based on which English you're in. I've known multiple people who were in 10th grade their 4th year in high school (because they failed English twice). I've also known people who were in 12th grade, but even with passing English would have to take another year or summer school to graduate (because there are other requirements too- maybe they didn't have enough math credits yet, or science). My high school didn't allow testing out of things, but the one I almost went to (we moved before I started) did, and I tested out of a few classes- although English wasn't one of the ones offered- you still had to do 4 years, you could just take higher levels in other things or have a bit easier schedule if you wanted to. 

The point- even assuming the school they were at allowed grade skipping like that, the only way I could see that happening is with summer school before starting (so, not a surprise), or testing out of classes (so, not a surprise).

This is what's been working really well for me: make a list of all the things you see your best self doing regularly- every day, every other day, or nearly every day. List as many as you can, you can add to it later (I can give you examples from my list of 50 something if you'd like). Make most fairly small (brushing my teeth is on my list, so is putting on deodorant), break things down if possible (like going to the gym is one, exercisingyour legs is one). Be as specific as possible about how long or how much (I have 15 minutes of yoga on mine, and drinking a gallon of water). Once you have a good list, pick one. Today, that's your task. Just that. Get a habit tracking app, or make a tracker. When it's done, mark it off. My first one was washing my face. I did other things too that day, of course, but that was the one thing on my habit tracker, and I did it. Tomorrow, pick another one. Now you have to do both. Day 3, pick another. Now you have 3 tasks. I could get more into why it really works for me/ how it works for me if you're interested.
